command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: POST/GET/DELETE matches the title but materially extends the Master GET-only Procedure; free-form privileges, `-k`, embedded credentials and deletion without an account-dependency oracle are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After baseline and approval, POST one allow-listed least-privilege role, verify exact fields and no account assignment, DELETE it once, then compare both role and account inventories to baseline.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the case as an atomic authorization-object lifecycle whose commit and cleanup are validated against both Roles and Accounts.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the GET/lifecycle conflict explicit and adds privilege allow-listing, capacity, account references, one-shot ambiguity handling and dual-inventory restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers one temporary custom role only; it does not validate existing roles, account login behavior or role assignment.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may not support custom roles or may retain audit references after deletion; unsupported behavior is reported, not worked around by changing existing roles.

project_override_considerations: If custom role creation is unsupported, do not substitute edits to built-in roles. If the platform auto-normalizes privilege ordering, compare sets semantically while retaining the raw hash.
expected_evidence: Recorded POST lifecycle versus GET-only Procedure conflict
Single POST status and exact role readback
Unchanged existing privileges/accounts and preserved security logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items require POST Role Creation/Deletion, but the Master Procedure sends only GET to list Roles. Collection readability cannot satisfy create/delete behavior, so the method and coverage conflict is material.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The schema, privilege set, unique ID, account dependency, approval and cleanup are identifiable prerequisites, making this REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a read-only Roles listing from masquerading as lifecycle coverage and constrains the real mutation to a dependency-free least-privilege role with verified removal.
independent_technical_reasoning: A role is shared authorization policy, so deletion safety depends on account references, not merely whether the role can be created. The exact privilege set must come from a firmware allow-list and security approval; free-form input can silently grant broad management rights. POST and DELETE ambiguity cannot be retried blindly because the object may already exist or be gone. Both Roles and Accounts inventories are needed before and after to prove the temporary role was isolated and cleanup caused no collateral authorization change.
